I've moved the FFmpeg path setting from the editor to the project settings to fix build issues.

I think there should be a way to disable the importer if the user wants to use an external video player addon. I don't know if it should be a project setting or if the addons can take over the importer by themselves.

Imports of big video files can be slow and the editor freezes. I'm not sure if that's a problem that should be fixed and what would be the best way to fix it.

>I've moved the FFmpeg path setting from the editor to the project settings to fix build issues.

It should be an editor setting in my opinion, otherwise you have to set it for every project. If there are build errors, you must have missed something.

> Importer is editor-only, so it should be moved to the `editor` folder, and `SCsub` will include it in editor build.

That was my first thought but I saw the Vorbis importer isn't editor-only and I guessed there was some use for the importers out of the editor.

You're right that having the setting in the editor settings makes more sense, I just lost the global view while fighting with the code.

> Also, please change config.py to generate the importer docs in doc_classes folder.

OK. Thanks.

I've exported the project and the OGV files aren't exported. I thought that after having added them as dependencies they would automatically be included, but that hasn't happened. I'll need some expert help.

Then there are two remaining tasks more related to the UI, the interaction with video player addons, and if it's OK to freeze the editor for the duration of the import. I would need some guidance.

I'll see if I can find some bandwidth to look at this during the Godot Engine 4.6 cycle.

Edit:

It's pretty cool.

Just to confirm, because the description doesn't explain what this PR actually does...

From what I understand, this adds importer support for mp4/webm/mpg/mpeg/mkv/avi/mov/wmv/qoi extensions? This is pretty innovative and should make videos much easier to use in Godot

They are transcoded into OGV using some configurable bitrate setting in the importer which is nice and flexible.

I assume the user is responsible for installing FFmpeg in order for this to work. There is a lot of UX work needed to guide the user to install FFmpeg since we had to do this work in FBX2glTF

i do wonder if this wouldn't be better as an asset lib addon, since then it could come with a LGPL build of FFmpeg for all the platforms (side note: important to build LGPL and not GPL. GPL code is not needed to *decode* h264).
Even if we go forward with including this in the engine, it should be possible to distribute ffmpeg on the asset lib or have a auto download button like we did for FBX2glTF, except the ffmpeg license is much better and safer than the autodesk license so I think we can streamline this

there is something about registering a new extension .theoravideostr which I don't understand... why can't we use whatever .ogv already does, for example read .ogv directly (I assume there would be a ResourceFormatLoader)?
EDIT: I understand why you want a separate resource type since it precludes needing to load the whole video file in memory. My question is just why does this require a different file extension compared to the existing OGV importer

also this PR affects the stop function to call seek(0) which really should be its own PR and bugfix for whatever it is fixing.

> Just to confirm, because the description doesn't explain what this PR actually does...

Yes, sorry, I will improve the description.

> From what I understand, this adds importer support for mp4/webm/mpg/mpeg/mkv/avi/mov/wmv/qoi extensions? This is pretty innovative and should make videos much easier to use in Godot

Those are the extensions that I thought would be interesting to have, but it could be any format supported by FFmpeg.

> They are transcoded into OGV using some configurable bitrate setting in the importer which is nice and flexible.

Yes, somewhat. Not a bitrate, but a quality setting as used commonly in VBR codecs. It can also scale the video and replace the alpha channel with a color.

> I assume the user is responsible for installing FFmpeg in order for this to work. There is a lot of UX work needed to guide the user to install FFmpeg since we had to do this work in FBX2glTF

Yes, the user should have FFmpeg already installed. Installing FFmpeg is actually very easy, it's a matter of unzipping a file, setting the path in Godot and done.

> i do wonder if this wouldn't be better as an asset lib addon, since then it could come with a LGPL build of FFmpeg for all the platforms (side note: important to build LGPL and not GPL. GPL code is not needed to _decode_ h264). Even if we go forward with including this in the engine, it should be possible to distribute ffmpeg on the asset lib or have a auto download button like we did for FBX2glTF, except the ffmpeg license is much better and safer than the autodesk license so I think we can streamline this

I like the flexibility of being able to install any FFmpeg version. I don't think licenses are a problem when the user installs it since we're not linking any code, but just running an external command. At the same time, I agree with anything that users find easier to use it.

> there is something about registering a new extension .theoravideostr which I don't understand... why can't we use whatever .ogv already does, for example read .ogv directly (I assume there would be a ResourceFormatLoader)? EDIT: I understand why you want a separate resource type since it precludes needing to load the whole video file in memory. My question is just why does this require a different file extension compared to the existing OGV importer

I think the current OGV importer doesn't use any resource file, it uses the video file directly. Maybe I could do the same, it's the first time I'm looking at the resource system and there are still some things I don't fully understand. I'll take a look at the way OGV files are imported and maybe I can do something similar.

> also this PR affects the stop function to call seek(0) which really should be its own PR and bugfix for whatever it is fixing.

Yes, I agree. For easier testing I prefer to keep it here, and I will create a new PR with only that fix. I just didn't get to do it yet.

Re-importing a file being used in a scene calls `VideoStreamPlayback::stop()` and that would call `seek`. That `seek` call when reloading the resource in the re-import process isn't needed, and freezes the editor. Moving the `seek` to `VideoStreamPlayer::stop()` fixes this issue, and it's in accordance with  the API docs.

> also this PR affects the stop function to call seek(0) which really should be its own PR and bugfix for whatever it is fixing.

We can probably speedly review the stop/seek bugfix if it's in a separate pr. If it's in this pull request, we'll have to wait for this to be complete which will delay the merge.

I hope I've written a proper PR description now.

I've created the PR for the `seek(0)` issue. I knew it should be done, but I wanted to avoid having this PR depending on another PR for now. I will keep the fix here so testers don't need to worry about it, and as soon as the other PR gets merged I'll rebase this one.
I mistakenly had thought there was some kind of qoi animated format but there's not, so qoi is removed. I wanted to include more lossless codecs, FFmpeg already supports FFv1 inside MKV though.

> there is something about registering a new extension .theoravideostr which I don't understand... why can't we use whatever .ogv already does, for example read .ogv directly (I assume there would be a ResourceFormatLoader)? EDIT: I understand why you want a separate resource type since it precludes needing to load the whole video file in memory. My question is just why does this require a different file extension compared to the existing OGV importer

I've been able to use the OGV file as the resource and now it exports correctly. I guess you were right. I still don't completely understand the magic behind it but it's great. Thanks @lyuma.

The basic functionality is working now, I just need some more help to know what else would be needed to be worth merging and useful.

I believe an extra String import option for additional custom import arguments could be valuable.

Unrelated to this, PR in particular, i have noticed in a project, that when i converted a file with my windows ffmpeg with certain arguents, didn't produce the exact same ogv as another guy who was importing it from Linux (mine was glitchy)
I am concerned this feature could hide this fact and people would rely conversion will jsut work for everyone because it works in their machine and then when some CICD exports a project it will create a broken vid.
Toughts?

> I am concerned this feature could hide this fact and people would rely conversion will jsut work for everyone because it works in their machine and then when some CICD exports a project it will create a broken vid.

This is already an issue with other importers that rely on external programs to work (namely, `.blend` import).

We can probably figure out ways to better to document the requirements if relevant for the current project, e.g. by displaying a notice on the Export dialog.

> I believe an extra String import option for additional custom import arguments could be valuable.

Yes, this could be an option. I'll add it if there's no objection.

> Unrelated to this, PR in particular, i have noticed in a project, that when i converted a file with my windows ffmpeg with certain arguents, didn't produce the exact same ogv as another guy who was importing it from Linux (mine was glitchy) I am concerned this feature could hide this fact and people would rely conversion will jsut work for everyone because it works in their machine and then when some CICD exports a project it will create a broken vid. Toughts?

This should be very unusual unless the FFmpeg version (or linked libraries) were different. And when it happens it's just bugs like any software can have. This PR doesn't change anything, you have already run into the issue just using FFmpeg by yourself. How are we hiding anything?

Yay! The [patch that adds a speed level option to FFmpeg](/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commit/3cd4fa9b895a359cf8c895f601c0016aae8b2c8f) has just been merged. I've added the option to this importer and set the fastest speed (`4`) as default. Imports will be faster but files will be also much bigger. Maybe speed `3` would be a better default since it compresses a lot better while still being half as fast. We can decide after testing.

This setting alleviates the issue with slow imports freezing the editor. The new option will be available in the FFmpeg builds since today. When using a build that doesn't have the option yet, it will be ignored. I had thought about adding a warning to the import tab when the FFmpeg version used doesn't support this option, but I have to learn how to add warnings to import tabs.

I've added a setting to write custom FFmpeg options after the input file and before the automatic options. The order of the arguments matters but I think this could be enough.

I've checked the [FBX2glTF download code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/e93d991329df7489e77ae4c9d3d686d8c1087dec) and it looks like a good solution. The user would be able to download the FFmpeg binary directly from us so we would have control of the version that is used. Advanced users could still change it to a custom binary.

>  I had thought about adding a warning to the import tab when the FFmpeg version used doesn't support this option, but I have to learn how to add warnings to import tabs.

I'm not sure if warnings are supported in the Import dock, but you can print a warning on import if the speed setting is not the default and the user is using a FFmpeg version that doesn't support it.

> - [ ] Create asset library addon or automation to install FFmpeg?

I think we could gain from having built-in installers for external tools in the editor, but it might be worth creating a general implementation that could be reused for all external tools. I'll look into opening a proposal for this.

**Edit:** Someone opened a proposal for another external tool a few hours before I wrote this comment:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12830

> > * [ ]  Create asset library addon or automation to install FFmpeg?
> 
> I think we could gain from having built-in installers for external tools in the editor, but it might be worth creating a general implementation that could be reused for all external tools. I'll look into opening a proposal for this.

Yes, that would be much better than reinventing the wheel every time. If we're heading that path then I'll remove the task from the list.

The other open question is if there's something that can be done about the slow imports. The Encoding Speed setting already helps but there will always be slow imports.

I've implemented a project setting to disable the importer since I don't think there's another way to make it compatible with video player addons.

> Can we change ffmpeg to prefer hardware encoding?

Hardware Theora encoding isn't a thing. If it was, it would have lower quality than software encoding (this is common to all hardware encoders out there, e.g. x264 vs NVENC).

That said, I'm surprised software Theora encoding is so slow. Is it using multiple threads currently? I didn't have time to test this PR yet.
Would we accept an av1 decoder in core?

> Would we accept an av1 decoder in core?

We don't have support for AV1 playback yet, but on a purely functional level, I would personally welcome it. However, one issue is that AV1 decoders have a large binary size and are complex to build. Some of them are also written in Rust, and we don't want to impose users to install a Rust toolchain to build Godot. It's probably best implemented as a GDExtension for the time being.

Keep in mind software AV1 decoding is demanding on the CPU, and is only viable on desktop platforms. Even then, it won't be great for battery life on laptops. Ideally, we would use something like [Vulkan Video](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6409) to access the system's hardware AV1 decoder, but Vulkan Video support is rather poor and it lacks equivalents in Direct3D 12 and Metal.

> That said, I'm surprised software Theora encoding is so slow. Is it using multiple threads currently? I didn't have time to test this PR yet.

No. I read there was an experimental implementation of a multithread encoder based on libtheora 1.0 but it was never merged.

Edit: About the slowness, it depends on many factors, quality settings, and resolution and length of the video. It also depends on the speed of the decoding process. For short videos at low/medium resolutions it shouldn't be an issue. I'm preparing for the worst. I'll like to hear your opinions when you test it.

I was looking into https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_video_samples and trying to see what we can do. Here's a copy of their readme focusing on AV1.

# decoder

1. Extracts (DEMUX via FFMPEG) compressed video from .mp4, .mkv, .mov and others video containers using AV1 compression formats.
2. The HW video decoder processes textures to Vulkan Video Images that can be directly sampled from Vulkan Samplers (Textures).
3. Using ffmpeg converts the YCbCr (YUV) Images to RGB while sampling the decoded images using the [VK_KHR_sampler_ycbcr_conversion](https://www.khronos.org/registry/vulkan/specs/1.2-extensions/man/html/VK_KHR_sampler_ycbcr_conversion.html)

# encoder

The upstream sample says this is work in progress.

1. use the Vulkan video encoding extensions to drive the HW-accelerated video encoder
2. this application encodes YCbCr content
3. AV1 compressed video to a file.

# Edited

Does anyone know the legal issues using hardware encoders and hardware decoders for av1, hevc and mp4?

> Does anyone know the legal issues using hardware encoders and hardware decoders for av1, hevc and mp4?

Using operating system APIs directly should be fine, but it's just a question of maintenance of all this platform-specific code. The codecs would not need to be part of Godot, so there would not be a license issue for the codecs themselves.

If we want to use an existing library, then it's a question of vendoring those libraries and using their license. Using FFmpeg is not an option but only because FFmpeg is LGPL.
I posted a proposal about using Windows Media Foundation libraries on Windows. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12864 and has a link to a Godot Engine branch.
@fire @lyuma Why bundle a library or bundle FFmpeg? Why not require the user to supply their own FFmpeg executabe, like this PR already does, and like we are already doing with Blender?
